$comment: Single source of truth for Loom label semantics (#10013). Embedded in loom-daemon; the Loom block of .github/labels.yml and defaults/.github/labels.yml is GENERATED from this file by `loom-daemon labels generate`. Edit here, then run `loom-daemon labels generate --write`.

stale_after_minutes, lifecycle and propagate are INERT in this slice: no consumer reads them yet (the daemon's own constants remain authoritative). contradicts_approval is the 1-based report order of labels that contradict loom:pr (null = does not contradict).
yaml_header: # LOOM-MANAGED BLOCK — everything between the BEGIN/END LOOM LABELS markers is
# owned by Loom and is refreshed wholesale on every install/upgrade; edits made
# in here WILL be lost. To add your repo's own labels, put them OUTSIDE this
# block (above the BEGIN marker or below the END marker) — the installer and
# uninstaller only ever touch the marked range, so your labels are preserved
# across install, upgrade, and uninstall. See #4187.
# These labels coordinate the Loom AI agent workflow
# Sync with: .loom/scripts/sync-labels.sh (from the installed repo root)
# Or manually: gh label create/edit commands
#   THIS FILE IS GENERATED from defaults/labels.json (the label registry, the
#   single source of truth for label semantics). Do NOT edit it by hand: edit
#   defaults/.github/labels.yml (the installer template copied into fresh
#   installs) are both generated and therefore BYTE-IDENTICAL. CI enforces it
#   label_registry unit tests — the build fails on any drift.

labels.name: loom:triage
labels.description: New issue awaiting Curator enhancement. Applied by: humans or any agent filing an issue (intake).
labels.applied_by: humans or any agent filing an issue (intake)
yaml_preamble: # Core Workflow States

labels.name: loom:issue
labels.description: Approved for work. Applied by: humans, Champion, sweep gate, Curator (starred) — see curator.md.

labels.name: loom:building
labels.description: Builder is implementing this issue. Applied by: Builder only (claim label).
yaml_preamble: # DEPRECATED: loom:in-progress removed (use role-specific labels)
# - loom:building (Builder implementing issue)
# - loom:curating (Curator enhancing issue)
# - loom:reviewing (Judge reviewing PR)
# - loom:treating (Doctor fixing bug/PR feedback)
# PR verdict-label mutual exclusion (#4570): {loom:review-requested,
# loom:reviewing, loom:changes-requested, loom:pr} form a mutually-exclusive
# verdict class on a PR — at most ONE of these four should be present at a
# time, with one legal transient exception: `loom:review-requested` and
# `loom:reviewing` may coexist while a Judge's claim is active (the review is
# in progress but has not yet produced a verdict). `loom:changes-requested`
# and `loom:pr` are terminal verdicts and must never coexist with each other,
# nor with a live `loom:reviewing` claim from a DIFFERENT actor's concurrent
# review. A PR observed carrying `loom:pr` + `loom:changes-requested` (or,
# equally invalid, `loom:pr` + `loom:review-requested` — twelve open PRs were
# found in this state on 2026-08-28, #7018) simultaneously is in an off-graph,
# contradictory state (see the PR #4560 incident, 2026-07-30) that must never
# be auto-merged — Champion's Verdict-State Janitor
# (defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md) resolves it fail-safe
# (`loom:pr` always loses; whichever OTHER label is present wins), and
# Judge/Doctor's Verdict-Time CAS Recheck (judge.md / doctor.md) is the
# write-time guard that prevents it from being produced in the first place.
# `verdict-staleness-guard.sh` and `loom-daemon`'s `reconcile_pr_verdicts`
# both strip EVERY terminal verdict label on a stale-verdict clear, not just
# the one they detected as stale, so a stray copy of the other cannot survive
# that transition either (#7018).
# PR verdict labels are SHA-scoped (#5686): `loom:changes-requested` and
# `loom:pr` are statements about the specific tree they were rendered against,
# not about the PR as an object. Judge stamps every verdict comment with
# `<!-- loom:verdict-sha sha=<head-sha> verdict=approved|changes-requested -->`,
# and once the PR's head SHA moves (rebase, force-push, or new commits) that
# verdict is STALE: it is cleared and the PR returns to `loom:review-requested`
# for a fresh evaluation. Enforced by defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh
# (called from judge.md's Stale-Verdict Sweep, doctor.md's Stale-Verdict Check,
# and champion-pr-merge.md's Verdict-State Janitor Part 2) with an always-on
# daemon backstop in loom-daemon's claim_reconciliation `reconcile_pr_verdicts`
# pass. A stale APPROVAL is the dangerous direction — before #5686 it let
# Champion auto-merge a tree no Judge had reviewed. A verdict carrying no marker
# at all (written before this convention) fails safe: it is kept, never
# force-cleared.
# Role-Specific Workflow Labels

labels.name: loom:curating
labels.description: Curator is enhancing this issue. Applied by: Curator only (claim label).

labels.name: loom:treating
labels.description: Doctor is fixing this bug or PR. Applied by: Doctor. Stale after LOOM_STALE_TREATING_MINUTES (60m).

labels.name: loom:reviewing
labels.description: Judge is reviewing this PR. Applied by: Judge only. Stale after LOOM_STALE_REVIEWING_MINUTES (30m).

labels.name: loom:evaluating
labels.description: Champion is evaluating this proposal (claim label, stale after 15m). Applied by: Champion only.

labels.name: loom:review-requested
labels.description: PR ready for Judge to review. Applied by: Builder when opening PR.

labels.name: loom:changes-requested
labels.description: PR requires changes before re-review (Judge requested modifications). Applied by: Judge.

labels.name: loom:merge-conflict
labels.description: PR has merge conflicts requiring resolution

labels.name: loom:sequenced
labels.description: Approved, but sequenced behind another PR. Applied by: the sequencing pass or an operator.
labels.applied_by: the sequencing pass or an operator
labels.color_note: yellow-700 - a scheduling hold, one shade apart from the in-progress ambers and the operator orange
yaml_preamble: # loom:sequenced (#9378) is the durable "approved, but not yet" ordering hold:
# NOT an escalation (loom:operator means a human must rule; a landing order
# does not) and NOT loom:blocked (an issue-status label that is not a merge
# gate). The label is refused by merge-pr.sh's verdict-contradiction guard
# beside loom:pr, with the same no-override treatment. The condition it waits
# on lives in a trusted `<!-- loom:sequence after=… pred_head=… follower_head=…
# plan=… -->` marker on the PR, evaluated by `loom-daemon merge-pr
# sequence-eval`; clearing is REMOVING THE LABEL once the recorded predecessor
# has landed at the recorded head — a mechanical condition, never a memory.

labels.name: loom:auto-merge-ok
labels.description: Override a Champion merge-risk hold (applied by Judge or human)

labels.name: loom:ci-failure
labels.description: PR has failing CI checks

labels.name: loom:pr
labels.description: PR approved by Judge, ready for Champion auto-merge. Applied by: Judge.

labels.name: loom:architect
labels.description: Architect proposal awaiting user approval. Applied by: Architect only.

labels.name: loom:blocked

yaml_preamble: # Status Labels

labels.name: loom:urgent
labels.description: Retired (#9244): use loom:operator-priority

labels.name: loom:abort
labels.description: Signal to abort the sweep for this issue (returns to loom:issue)

labels.name: loom:operator-only
labels.description: Requires human action or ruling outside automation (creds, infra, hardware); sweep skips
yaml_preamble: # loom:operator-only vs loom:blocked: operator-only = a human must act or rule
# OUTSIDE automation (credentials, infra, hardware, or an owner-gated decision
# on owner-tracked code) and sweep skips it entirely;
# blocked = waiting on a dependency but otherwise automatable. Keep the
# description at/under GitHub's 100-char label-description limit so sync-labels.sh
# can create it (a longer description fails with HTTP 422 and the label never syncs).

labels.name: loom:needs-capability
labels.description: Blocked on a missing tool/agent capability, not operator-by-right; link the capability-request issue
labels.color_note: amber-200 - distinct from the operator-only orange family
yaml_preamble: # loom:needs-capability (#5817): a narrower claim than loom:operator-only —
# blocked on a missing tool/agent capability, not an operator-by-right
# decision. Skips sweep identically to loom:operator-only today (same
# hard-skip rows in sweep.md and the same warn-operator-gated.sh
# dependency-declared check); the routing convention for when to apply this
# vs. loom:operator-only is out of scope here (see #5818). Keep the
# description at/under GitHub's 100-char label-description limit — see the
# comment above loom:operator-only.

labels.name: loom:operator-blocked
labels.description: operator-only sub-kind: self-clearing, waiting on a named issue/infra to land
labels.color_note: orange-300 - lightest: transient, expected to clear on its own
yaml_preamble: # loom:operator-only sub-kind labels (#5671). A single `loom:operator-only` was
# carrying at least four meanings with no mechanical way to tell them apart —
# these four ALWAYS accompany `loom:operator-only` (never replace it; every
# existing filter/skip that keys off the base label is unaffected) and record
# WHICH kind at the point of application. Exactly one of the four is applied
# per issue/PR. See .loom/docs/label-state-machine.md "operator-only sub-kinds"
# for the full decision table and the machine-readable-blocker convention.
# NOTE (#5826): loom:operator-decision is no longer the safe unsure-default —
# being unsure is a sign the analysis is incomplete, not a reason to apply the
# label. Only apply loom:operator-only once a specific sub-kind fits.
# NOTE (#6881, updated #6893): loom:operator-mechanical's "no judgement
# required" describes the WORK. The base loom:operator-only label's hard skip
# still wins for every sub-kind by default -- with ONE narrow, fail-closed
# exception since #6893: a mechanical item whose body declares
# `<!-- loom:capability=<name> -->` marker(s) (#6892) that the executing HOST
# holds (LOOM_WORKER_CAPABILITIES, env-only) is routed to a PROPOSE-ONLY lane
# instead of parked -- it emits the commands / a PR for an operator to
# approve, never a live credentialed action. The other three sub-kinds are
# unchanged and hard-skip unconditionally, marker or no marker.

labels.name: loom:operator-mechanical
labels.description: operator-only sub-kind: no judgement needed; parks unless a declared capability is held (#6893)
yaml_preamble: # A loom:operator-mechanical item may additionally declare the capability(ies)
# it needs via `<!-- loom:capability=<name> -->` marker(s) in its body (#6892)
# -- meaningful only alongside THIS sub-kind, ignored by the other three. See
# .loom/docs/label-state-machine.md "Capability-declaration convention" for
# the closed vocabulary and parser contract, and its "Dispatch path (#6893)"
# subsection for the four gates that consume it.

labels.name: loom:operator-decision
labels.description: operator-only sub-kind: preference/authority axis named; not a safe default (#5826)

labels.name: loom:decision-malformed
labels.description: operator-decision bounced for missing/invalid decision block; Curator repairs or re-routes (#10057)

labels.name: loom:operator-objective
labels.description: operator-only sub-kind: determined once operator states objective; lists candidates
labels.color_note: orange-200 - lightest of all: clears on a single stated preference

labels.name: loom:operator
labels.description: Engine stops work on this item; human is the only transition out. Sweep/shepherd do not skip it.
labels.applied_by: Champion (merge-risk and critical-file holds); merge-pr.sh #8508 escalation
labels.color_note: orange-600 - operator-action signal, one shade darker than operator-only
yaml_preamble: # loom:operator is the first-class "a human is needed" pipeline state (#5502):
# the engine (any role, plus sweep/shepherd dispatch) will not act on this
# item further until a human does. It differs from BOTH neighbors above:
# vs. loom:operator-only — operator-only tells sweep/shepherd to SKIP the item
# entirely; loom:operator does not — the item stays in the normal
# re-evaluation queue so a role's own exit rule (e.g. Champion's head-SHA
# precheck, an explicit human comment, or a new artifact) can still clear it
# automatically. vs. loom:blocked — blocked means "waiting on a dependency,
# still automatable"; loom:operator means "the engine has stopped and only a
# human moves it forward." See .loom/docs/label-state-machine.md for the full
# entry/exit model.
# Applied by: Champion (merge-risk and critical-file holds), and by
# merge-pr.sh's #8508 escalation when the #8248 required-check freshness guard
# blocks a merge that its own automated re-date remedy could not unblock
# (defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md). Removed by a human.

labels.name: loom:operator-priority
labels.description: Land ASAP, ahead of all other work (not a hold). Applied by: humans, directly or via loom-ui star.
labels.applied_by: humans, directly or via loom-ui star
yaml_preamble: # loom:operator-priority (#9244) is the operator's "star": land this ASAP,
# ahead of all other work, fleet-wide. It is NOT loom:operator (the hold
# above) and it is NOT a hold of any kind -- nothing may treat a
# `loom:operator` / `loom:operator-` prefix match as a hold without excluding
# this label by name (see loom-daemon pr_latency::hold_labels). The daemon's
# work finder sorts starred issues first (by when they were starred), lists
# them even outside loom:issue (triage, curated, or unlabelled; the sweep then
# starts from Curator), and may run one starred sweep over the concurrency
# cap. Skip/park labels still win: a starred issue carrying loom:blocked,
# loom:operator-only, loom:operator-decision or loom:operator is never
# dispatched. Applied by: humans (directly or via the loom-ui star). Removed
# by: humans.

labels.name: loom:operator-high-priority
labels.description: Level 2, above the star (capped, not a hold). Applied by: humans, directly or via loom-ui.
labels.color_note: amber-700 - one shade above the star
yaml_preamble: # loom:operator-high-priority (#10307) is operator priority LEVEL 2, the
# double star: above loom:operator-priority, which it nests over (level >= 2
# counts as starred everywhere; a level-2 item need not also carry the star).
# Every starred-first pass drains by effective level, highest first. Capped:
# at most 5 open issues fleet-wide by default (loom-ui enforces the cap at
# click time; the daemon reports an over-cap level in the star-liveness
# digest and never refuses a human's label). Its open blockers inherit the
# level as loom:high-priority-inherited. Like the star it is NOT a hold:
# every loom:operator- prefix match must exclude it by name. Applied by:
# humans (directly or via the loom-ui double star). Removed by: humans.

labels.name: loom:high-priority-inherited
labels.description: Blocks a level-2 issue, so treated as level 2. Applied by: loom-daemon star-liveness only.
labels.color_note: amber-600 - the double star's shade, lighter
yaml_preamble: # loom:high-priority-inherited (#10307) is DERIVED, never a human's or a
# role's: the daemon's star-liveness pass writes it on every open issue that
# blocks a loom:operator-high-priority issue, directly or transitively (across
# managed repos), with a provenance comment naming the source, and removes it
# once no level-2 source reaches the issue. Every reader treats it exactly
# like level 2. It never counts toward the level-2 cap and is never accepted
# from a loom-ui intent. Applied by / removed by: the loom-daemon
# star-liveness pass only.

labels.description: Multi-phase epic proposal (decomposes into implementation issues)

labels.name: loom:heavy
labels.description: CPU/RAM-intensive sweep; refused on local-dev host_class. Applied by: humans/Curator/Architect.
yaml_preamble: # loom:heavy (#9034): the mechanical "heavy" signal the host-class gate refuses
# on a host_class: local-dev machine (autonomous.workFinder.hostClass) unless
# explicitly overridden (--allow-local / allowHeavyLocal). A resource-weight
# axis, deliberately NOT the same thing as the tier:* priority axis above.

labels.name: external
labels.description: Non-collaborator submission; needs maintainer approval before curation. Applied by: humans only.
yaml_preamble: # External Contribution Gate
# Not part of the loom: workflow. A non-collaborator submission needs maintainer
# approval before Curator/Builder process it.
# This is a HARD EXCLUSION (#7528): no Loom role may curate, build, or promote
# it, AND loom-daemon's work finder will not dispatch a sweep for it. The
# authoritative list lives in ONE place — `defaults/scripts/hard-exclusion-labels.sh`
# (mirrored by `loom_daemon::hard_exclusion::HARD_EXCLUSION_LABELS`, kept in
# lockstep by a unit test). Adding a hard exclusion means editing that list, not
# just adding a label here.
